title: Two of the four action renderers still absorb unknown keys silently — an object spread disables the excess-property check that #4046 just installed
body:
Found while implementing #4046 (step 3 — deleting `ActionDef`'s `[key: string]: any`). Filed rather than fixed: out of that card's scope.

## What #4046 bought, and where it does not apply

#4046 closed `ActionDef`, so a key the interface does not declare is now a `TS2353` at any site that authors an action literal. That guarantee holds at two of the four action renderers and **not** at the other two, for a reason unrelated to `ActionDef` itself.

TypeScript only applies the excess-property (freshness) check to a *fresh* object literal. An object literal containing a spread of a non-literal value loses that freshness, so unknown keys in it are accepted. Two of the four `execute({ … })` forward literals contain such a spread:

| forward site | spread in the literal | unknown key |
|---|---|---|
| `action-button.tsx:96` | `...paramsPayload` | **absorbed** |
| `action-icon.tsx:71` | `...localContext` | **absorbed** |
| `action-group.tsx:238` | none | rejected (TS2353) |
| `action-menu.tsx:218` | none | rejected (TS2353) |

## Measured, twice, in opposite directions

**Direction 1 — the natural experiment.** Deleting the index signature produced exactly two `TS2353`s across the whole workspace, both for `description`: `action-group.tsx:246` and `action-menu.tsx:228`. `action-button.tsx:103` and `action-icon.tsx:78` forward *the same key in the same way* and reported nothing.

**Direction 2 — a direct probe.** Inserting an invented key into one site of each kind, then type-checking `@object-ui/components`:

```
src/renderers/action/action-menu.tsx(229,13): error TS2353: Object literal may only
specify known properties, and 'zzBogusKey2' does not exist in type 'ActionDef'.
```

One error, from the non-spread site. The identical insertion at `action-button.tsx:104` produced nothing. (Both probes reverted; they were measurement only.)

## Why this is worth a card

The renderers are the highest-traffic authoring boundary for an `ActionDef` — they are where `check:action-forward-parity` says the keys must be assembled, and the gate has caught six separate dropped-key defects there (`bodyExtra`, `bodyShape`, `resultDialog`, `openIn`/`locations`/`undoable`, `label`/`description`). #4046's whole premise is that a typo at such a site should be a compile error rather than a button that does nothing (objectstack#2169). At two of those four sites it still is not, and nothing says so — a reader who knows `ActionDef` is closed would reasonably assume it is closed everywhere.

Note the shape is not "the type is wrong". `ActionDef` is correct; the check is simply not applied. So no amount of further tightening on the type reaches this.

## Options, not a prescription

- Hoist the spread out of the literal — build the object, then spread into it at the end (`{ ...base, ...paramsPayload }` where `base` is annotated `ActionDef`), or annotate the literal's own binding. Cheapest; restores freshness where it was lost.
- Give `execute()` a parameter type that rejects excess keys structurally rather than by freshness.
- Extend `check:action-forward-parity` to also assert that each forward literal is checkable — it already parses these exact literals with the compiler API, so it is the natural home.

## Anchors

Verified on `origin/main` @ `4cb0562b5`, and again on the #4046 branch.

- `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-button.tsx` — literal at `:96`, spread `...paramsPayload` at `:110`
- `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-icon.tsx` — literal at `:71`, spread `...localContext`
- `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-group.tsx` — literal at `:238`, no spread
- `packages/components/src/renderers/action/action-menu.tsx` — literal at `:218`, no spread

Refs #4046, #4050, #4192, objectstack#2169.
